title: Prometheus sidecar patterns and log-sink Terraform notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for recommended Prometheus + OTEL sidecar patterns and Terraform module shape for private deployments (VPC and on‑prem Kubernetes). Goal is to capture a minimal, robust default that operators can adopt with clear upgrade and rollback instructions, plus practical TF inputs/outputs for the platform modules.

Context and constraints:
- Private deployments are often air‑gapped or have restricted egress; we must assume no direct internet access from collectors by default.
- Customers run a mix of k8s (EKS/vanilla k8s) and VM clusters; modules should be cluster-agnostic where possible.
- Security: all remote_write/logship traffic must use mTLS or customer PKI; Terraform modules need to surface cert/key secret names.
- Cost/complexity: prefer sidecar or per-pod collector for high-cardinality traces vs daemonset for uniform scraping depending on scale.

High-level recommended patterns (tradeoffs):
1) Sidecar OTEL + local Prometheus instance per node/pod group (pattern: sidecar-per-app)
   - Where: high-security, multi-tenant apps that require per-app isolation and richer spans.
   - Pros: per-app control, capture local logs/traces pre-network translation, easy to associate metadata.
   - Cons: more resource overhead, harder to manage at scale.
   - TF implications: expose resource quotas for per-pod sidecars and image overrides.

2) Centralized collector DaemonSet + Prometheus node exporter + kube-scrape relabel rules (pattern: daemonset-relay)
   - Where: cluster-level observability, many small services.
   - Pros: single place to control batching, retries, and remote_write. Lower per-pod overhead.
   - Cons: needs robust autoscaling for bursts, careful relabeling to preserve tenant separation.
   - TF implications: module should allow controlling daemonset resources, HPA config, and service-account/role bindings.

3) Gateway relay (in-cluster) + remote VPC egress gateway for multi-cluster aggregation (pattern: relay-gateway)
   - Where: customer wants a stable egress point and centralized control of IAM and TLS.
   - Pros: simplifies firewall rules, centralizes TLS termination, easier to whitelist.
   - Cons: single point of failure unless HA configured.
   - TF implications: expose LB/ALB config, security_group rules, ACM/cert manager integration inputs.

Prometheus topology recommendations:
- Scrape model: prefer kube-service discovery + pod annotations for most k8s workloads. Use static_config for VM targets.
- Remote write: always use an authenticated, encrypted remote_write to the platform ingress (or local relay); do not rely on direct push from sidecars unless inside secured VPC.
- Recording rules: keep a small set of OVERRIDE rules in the TF module for essential SLOs (request_latency: p50/p95/p99), and allow customers to add extra rules via configmap merging.

Terraform module sketch (observability/core):
- module name: observability_core
- purpose: deploy Prometheus (k8s manifests/Helm optional), Grafana, node-exporter, and collector baseline (daemonset or sidecar templates).
- required inputs (sample):
  - cluster_type: "k8s" | "vm"
  - prometheus_helm_chart: string (default pinned chart reference)
  - prometheus_values_overrides: string (yaml blob)
  - otel_collector_mode: "daemonset" | "sidecar" | "gateway"
  - otel_image: string
  - remote_write_endpoint: string (internal ingress url)
  - remote_write_auth_method: "mtls" | "bearer" | "aws_sigv4"
  - mTLS_cert_secret_name: string (optional)
  - log_sink_type: "s3" | "syslog" | "loki"
  - log_sink_config: string (yaml/blob)
  - prometheus_storage_class: string
  - retention_days: number
  - node_selector: map (as stringified JSON/YAML for TF compatibility)
- outputs (sample):
  - prometheus_endpoint: string
  - grafana_endpoint: string
  - otel_collector_daemonset_name: string
  - observability_tls_secret_id: string

Implementation notes and small TF snippets to consider including in module: (these are notes, not prescriptive)
- Use Helm provider for Prometheus but keep a plain-k8s manifest option for air-gapped installs. Provide both code paths behind a boolean.
- Store long-lived state in backend (S3/MinIO for onprem) with locking (DynamoDB or consul lock). Expose backend config as module variables.
- For mTLS: expect a Kubernetes Secret containing tls.crt/tls.key; module should create a Secret object if provided cert data or reference an existing one.

Example variable block (pseudo-TF expressed as text):
- variable "otel_collector_mode" { default = "daemonset" description = "collector: daemonset|sidecar|gateway" }
- variable "remote_write_endpoint" { description = "internal platform receiver endpoint" }

Log shipping patterns and concerns:
- S3 archival: use fluent-bit -> collector -> s3 plugin OR fluentd with buffering to avoid data loss. For air-gapped, use local fs buffer + batch upload to onprem object store (MinIO).
- Loki: when using Loki, prefer promtail as daemonset with label-based filtering to reduce cardinality.
- Syslog: for legacy appliances, run a fluent-bit forwarder to a central syslog-ng collector.
- TF module should expose a "log_buffer_size_mb" and "flush_interval_s" for runtime tuning.

Upgrade plan for OTEL collector and Prometheus Helm charts (draft):
1) Prepare:
   - Create a test namespace that mirrors production scrape configs and retention.
   - Build new collector image with required patches and publish to internal registry (or make available via airgap archive).
   - Add a feature flag variable in TF: otel_upgrade_campaign = "canary1"
2) Canary rollout:
   - If daemonset: scale daemonset to 1 node with taint and schedule canary pod; if sidecar: deploy a small canary deployment with identical config.
   - Monitor for 24–48 hours: metrics to watch: scrape_success_ratio, otel_exporter_errors_total, span_dropped_total, prometheus_remote_write_retries.
   - Run synthetic traffic via stress tool to generate traces/metrics and validate ingestion.
3) Rollout:
   - Gradual rollout using node selectors or pod labels (20% -> 50% -> 100%).
   - If using gateway pattern, update gateway in two AZs (or nodes) with blue/green swap.
4) Rollback:
   - Keep old collector images available. TF should support quick toggle back by setting otel_image to previous tag and applying.
   - Rehydrate previously archived logs if needed (S3).

Testing and validation checklist:
- End-to-end: generate traces + logs + metrics from app; verify they appear in Grafana and traces in chosen backend.
- Scrape validation: prometheus_targets{job=~".*"} shows up and up==1 for all expected targets.
- TLS verification: perform mTLS handshake tests using openssl s_client to remote_write_endpoint.
- Assert storage: retention policy is honored by listing TSDB blocks and checking oldest block timestamp.

Operational runbook snippets (quick actionable items):
- Collector OOMs: reduce sampling rate, increase memory request for daemonset/sidecar, offload heavy processors to gateway.
- High remote_write latency: enable batching and increase max-retries/backoff in exporter config; consider adding relay to reduce long-haul calls.
- Missing logs: check fluent-bit buffer path permissions and disk utilization; check s3/minio credentials in secret.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default: daemonset for k8s + sidecar opt-in for sensitive services, or sidecar-by-default for compliance customers? Document tradeoffs for sales.
- Should Terraform module validate cert expiry and rotate secrets automatically, or leave as ops task?
- Add an integration test harness in infra repo that spins up ephemeral k8s cluster and runs the canary validation flow.

References and links:
- Internal GH PR with initial helm values: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/312
- Example OTEL config used in tests: CONFLUENCE-OBSERVABILITY-243 (link above)
- Jira for rollout tracking: JIRA-OPS-1829

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc intentionally pragmatic; convert into a Confluence playbook once we settle on defaults.
- After first customer install, capture actual perf numbers (token throughput, remote_write requests per second, disk usage) to tune defaults.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-15: initial draft (Ava)
- 2024-11-22: added TF variable sketches and gateway notes (Diego)
- 2024-12-02: added upgrade/canary checklist and operational runbook (Rina)
